Hi Amy —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Attached is a short Mutual Action Plan (draft) that lays out the technical validation path we discussed and proposed deadlines for the pilot. High-level asks for the evaluation:

- Your target SLOs (p50/p95/p99 latency) and expected peak concurrency for booking flows.
- Sample traffic profile (payload sizes, average prompt length, QPS distribution).
- Primary acceptance criteria (latency threshold, quality checks, cost target).

From Redwood’s side we plan to run:
- TTFT (time-to-first-token) and token throughput at 1, 8, 32, 128 concurrent sessions.
- End-to-end latency (p50/p95/p99) measured with real-ish promptsets you provide and our standardized harness.
- Variant comparison across three catalog variants (smaller quantized, medium fp16, larger int8-style) with quality evals (ROUGE/semantic QA checks) and hallucination spot-checks.

Attached: Luma_MAP_draft_20270418.xlsx (MAP milestones + responsibilities).

—Camila

- p95 end-to-end latency under 450ms for the main booking prompt set
- TTFT under 120ms for the first token in the flow
- Latency degradation under 20% at 60 concurrent sessions

Date: 2027-04-20T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: evaluation plan + bench matrix for Luma (draft)

Team —

Putting the bench matrix and evaluation plan here so we can turn this around quickly once Amy confirms the traffic. Key points:

Test matrix (bench_matrix_20270420.csv attached):
- Workloads: booking_prompt_small (avg 40 tokens), booking_prompt_long (avg 140 tokens), summary_prompt (avg 280 tokens).
- Concurrency sweep: 1, 8, 32, 64, 128 sessions.
- Metrics captured: TTFT, token_throughput (tokens/sec), end_to_end_latency p50/p95/p99, CPU/GPU utilization, cost per 1M tokens.
- Model variants: redwood-s8-q4 (8B quantized), redwood-m30-fp16 (30B fp16), redwood-l70-int8 (70B int8 experiment).

Quality checks: run 500 sample prompts per variant, automated semantic similarity + 20 manual hallucination spot checks for each variant. We’ll calculate a quality/perf score to recommend default for production.

Acceptance & gating:
- Variant passes if p95 < 450ms and TTFT < 120ms at 25 concurrency and quality score within 5% of the baseline (redwood-m30-fp16 baseline).
- If none pass, propose staged rollouts with caching and prefix trimming or fall back to lower-latency model with additional cost offsets.

Timeline (draft):
- 4/21–4/22: run full concurrency sweep on synthetic + provided traffic
- 4/23: internal analysis and bench_results_summary draft
- 4/26: deliver MAP_final and recommended variant + SOW-ready numbers for procurement

Attachments: bench_matrix_20270420.csv

Camila

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-21T15:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Internal: evaluation plan + bench matrix for Luma (draft)

Quick sync — I ran the first synthetic sweep overnight and attached the preliminary PDF (latency_report_v1.pdf). Highlights:

- redwood-s8-q4 (8B quantized): TTFT median 95ms, p95 at 540ms under 25 concurrent sessions (miss on p95 target), throughput good and cost lowest. Quality checks show a 6.8% delta vs baseline on our semantic QA metric (smallest model loses ground on longer prompts).
- redwood-m30-fp16 (30B fp16): TTFT median 110ms, p95 420ms at 25 concurrent sessions (meets p95 and TTFT targets), best overall quality/balance.
- redwood-l70-int8 (70B int8): TTFT 160ms, p95 380ms at low concurrency but p95 climbs to 610ms at 64+ concurrent (GPU memory and kernel scheduling overheads). Quality marginally better than m30 but not enough to justify cost for this workload.

Recommendation: present medium (redwood-m30-fp16) as default for pilot. If Luma insists on lower-cost option, we can offer s8-q4 with a caveat and a 2-week canary to validate real-world quality.

Notes: we triggered a specific regression in ordering prompts for s8-q4 on long-context cases — flagged Rishi to look into a microarchitectural perf/precision tweak.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Principal Performance Engineer | Redwood Inference

Attachment: latency_report_v1.pdf (pdf)

Amy / team —

Appreciate the clarity on dates. Attached are the final artifacts we’ll hand over today: MAP_final_20270423.xlsx (mutual action plan with responsibilities and signoffs) and bench_results_summary_20270423.pdf (consolidated numbers + variant-quality tradeoff table). Summary decisions:

- Pilot model: redwood-m30-fp16 recommended as default for pilot (meets p95 & TTFT targets at 25 concurrency with good quality).
- Contingency: redwood-s8-q4 offered as low-cost canary if Luma signs tradeoff acknowledgement (higher p95 risk at 25+ concurrency and observed quality delta on long prompts).
- If pilot shows <5% quality regression and p95 < 500ms at production-ish traffic, we recommend a phased rollout with autoscaling and prefix caching enabled.

Confirmed timeline (mutual):
- 4/23: bench results delivered + MAP final (today)
- 4/26: Redwood delivers SOW-ready cost matrix for procurement (line-item costs for pilot + 3-month committed capacity)
- 5/01: Target PO/DocuSign complete (Procurement action)
- 5/03–5/17: 2-week technical canary (pilot)
- 5/24: Production handoff (assuming canary acceptance)

Action items for Redwood (owners):
- Finalize SOW and cost matrix (Camila) — due 4/26
- Fix s8-q4 ordering regression and rerun quick spot-checks (Rishi) — in parallel, target 4/25
- Canary run plan + monitoring dashboards (Marissa/Sean) — deliver pre-canary runbook by 4/30

Amy — once procurement confirms 5/01 PO target we’ll lock the pilot capacity. Would you like a 30-minute walkthrough of the bench_results_summary tomorrow to walk through tradeoffs for your stakeholders?

Best —
Camila
